description: Attacks each hypothesis with counter-evidence taken from the day's own fixture; a hypothesis that does not answer a serious objection dies here.

fixture.description: what `check-intake` established about this crossing's data: which day it is, where the four files are and how many rows each of them holds. It is the only node that touches the filesystem to find out, and every node after it reads the paths from here instead of assembling one.

trading_day.description: the fixture day this crossing runs against: `day-1`, `day-2` or `day-3`.

daily_figures.description: null when the file is missing or is not a JSON array at the top level.

broker_flow.description: null when the file is missing or is not a JSON array at the top level.

signals.description: null when the file is missing or is not a JSON array at the top level.

facts.description: null when the file is missing or is not a JSON array at the top level.

context.description: one entry per triaged signal: the recent trend, and any fact related to it.

trend.description: what the daily figures say about where this ticker has been: the move, the turnover against its own recent level, the number of trades.

figures_cited.description: the fields of `daily-figures.json` the trend rests on, by name.

related_facts.description: the entries of `facts.json` that touch this ticker or the whole session. Empty is a real answer: most signals have no fact beside them, and saying so is what stops the next node from inventing one.

hypotheses.description: one explanation per triaged signal — what would have to be true for it to be flow.

driver.description: the shape of the explanation. `undetermined` is a legal answer and a cheap one: a named driver nobody can cite is worse than an honest gap.

cited_context.description: the `signal_id`s and `fact_id`s this explanation rests on. An explanation citing nothing is a guess wearing a contract.

perguntas_respondidas.description: questions the founder has already answered on this work, so the new session does not reopen what was decided. An empty list is legal and is the common case. The key and the two names inside it are the CONTROL PLANE's projection vocabulary, not this bundle's — `packages/core/src/domain/context.ts` publishes them under these names for every registered manifest, and renaming them here would declare an input the projection never delivers (D20).

outcome.description: mandatory in every skill of role gate. In this graph "pass" follows the "survives" edge and "fail" the "dead" edge. "escalate_human" exists because the format demands the three values — a session that needs the founder PAUSES with an input-request instead of settling it here.

resultado.description: the label of the edge this node took. The GRAPH's vocabulary and not the skill's, which is why there is no enum here: the same skill can live under two graphs with different labels. Declared because the report protocol tells the session to return ONE block only, with the label INSIDE the object of the contract (t161, t259), and with `additionalProperties: false` an `output` that did not declare it would be refused whole — which is exactly how bundle 2 lost a triaged thesis before t260 and t276. The key itself stays spelled the way the result protocol reserves it (`packages/runner/src/dispatch/parse-node-result.ts`); its VALUES are this graph's edge labels, and those are English.

objections.description: one entry per objection raised, each with a severity and the hypothesis's answer — or `null` when there was none. An empty list is refused by the contract: a red team that found nothing did not run.

hypothesis_answer.description: `null` when the hypothesis has no answer to this objection.

counter_evidence.description: the evidence the red team brings against the hypotheses, drawn from the fixture and cited by file and record. It is NOT researched: every node of this bundle declares `network.allowed: false`, so a researched field would name a capability the manifest forbids itself. What replaces research here is reading the rest of the day — the figures and the facts the hypothesis did not look at.

file.description: which of the day's four fixture files the record comes out of.

record.description: which record inside that file: a `fact_id`, a `signal_id`, a ticker, a ticker and a broker. Enough for a reader to open the file and find the same row.

preconditions: `fixture.paths` names the day's files, so the counter-evidence can be cited to a record

checks.description: A gate verifies with evidence of its own: rereading the hypotheses and agreeing with them is not a red team. The defect to catch is the `survives` that coexists with a high-severity objection nobody answered.
checks.instruction:
Check the attack itself, not the hypotheses.

1. Does every entry of `counter_evidence` open at the file and record it cites, with the value it claims? Quote the row.
2. Was each hypothesis attacked on its OWN weakest point — the ordinary explanation it did not rule out — rather than on a generic doubt that would fit any of them?
3. Does any objection of `severity` `high` carry a `null` `hypothesis_answer` while the outcome is `pass`? That combination fails the check outright.

An empty `objections` list is refused by the contract; an `objections` list of formalities is refused here.

instructions:
# Try to kill each hypothesis with the day's own data

Your job is to knock these explanations down. You are not checking whether they
are well written; you are looking for the record in this day's fixture that
makes each one wrong.

## Where you are

You write no file at all. No node of this graph touches the target repository:
the result comes back **through the output contract**, and what records it is
the control plane. Reading, you read the fixture this class ships — and only
that. The network is closed on every node of this bundle (RF-28): there is no
research step here, and a claim you cannot cite to a fixture record is a claim
this graph has no place for.

**There is no research step here.** Every skill of this bundle declares
`network.allowed: false`, so counter-evidence you could only get from outside
is counter-evidence this graph forbids itself. What you have instead is the
rest of the day — the figures and the facts the hypothesis did not look at:

{{input.fixture.paths}}

The hypotheses to attack:

{{input.hypotheses}}

And the context they were built on:

{{input.context}}

## How to attack

For each hypothesis, go after the ordinary explanation it failed to rule out.
The four that kill most flow readings:

1. **The calendar.** Is there a fact in `facts.json` — an index-portfolio turn,
   a scheduled event — that already accounts for the move?
2. **One broker.** In `broker-flow.json`, does the whole net flow sit on a
   single house? Then it is a transaction, not a market reading.
3. **The auction.** Does the turnover concentrate at the close rather than
   across the session?
4. **The baseline.** In `daily-figures.json`, is the move actually large
   against this ticker's own recent level, or only against the exchange's?

Every objection carries a `severity` and the `hypothesis_answer` — or `null`
when the hypothesis has none. Every counter-evidence entry carries the `file`
and the `record` it comes from, so a reader can open the same row.

NEVER conclude `pass` (the `survives` edge) while an objection of `severity` `high` carries a `null` `hypothesis_answer`: an unanswered serious objection is what `dead` is for, and it is the cheapest death in this graph.

## What this graph is not

This is signal DETECTION, and the product is a reading of the flow with its
objections attached. Nothing you produce here is a trade instruction: no buy,
no sell, no price target, no expected return. The final node records process
metrics — did the intake pass, how many signals survived the triage, did the
red team run — because a market outcome is slow validation and never a round's
metric (D14, stated for bets and holding here for the same reason).

## When to escalate to the human

If you need the founder in order to finish, end your turn with exactly ONE
fenced block, and nothing after it:

```input-request
{"question": "<one or two sentences: what happened and why a decision is needed>",
 "context": "<the supporting detail — evidence, what you tried, the alternatives you weighed>",
 "options": ["<short action label>", "<short action label>"],
 "recommendation": "<the ONE action you would take, in the imperative>",
 "default": "<the option to apply if the founder simply accepts>"}
```

What belongs in each field:

- `question` is read first and has to stay short. State the decision, not the
  investigation that led to it.
- `context` is where ALL of your reasoning goes: the evidence, what you already
  tried, the alternatives you weighed and why you rejected each one. It may run
  long — the founder reads it in full in this session's own record.
- `recommendation` is an imperative action and nothing else. It is the text of a
  one-click accept button, so whatever you put there becomes the founder's
  answer, verbatim.
- `options` are short labels, each one a decision the founder could pick.
- `default` is what applies if the founder simply accepts.

Only `question` is required; omit any field that has nothing in it. Ask ONE
question, and do not repeat any of this as prose before or after the block —
the block is the whole message.

Emitting an `input-request` ends your work for now: whatever you have already
done is kept exactly as it is, the session pauses, and the answer reaches you
when it arrives. Do not wait, do not poll, and do not emit two blocks — a
request for a decision always supersedes a report of a result.

No node of this graph is obliged to escalate. There is no human-decision node
here: a radar that publishes a reading is not a desk that allocates capital,
and `escalate_human` exists in the gate enum because the format demands the
three values, not because this graph routes on it.

## What to return

`outcome`, `resultado`, `objections`, `counter_evidence`, `note`.

- `outcome: "pass"` with `resultado: "survives"` — at least one hypothesis
  answered its serious objections. The executor follows the **survives** edge,
  on to the brief, and the objections travel with it.
- `outcome: "fail"` with `resultado: "dead"` — nothing survived. The executor
  follows the **dead** edge, straight to the scorecard. That is a red team
  working, not a session failing.
- `outcome: "escalate_human"` exists because the gate format demands the three
  values.
